item: 9.1 Temporary Sign By-law and Election Sign By-law Updates
text: WHEREAS Ajax Council has implemented a number of changes to Town by-laws in recent years to improve compliance with temporary and election sign regulations, including making investments in a new proactive enforcement program, in an effort to address waste, sightline issues on roadways, and other nuisance issues; AND WHEREAS enforcement of these by-laws continues to require considerable time and effort from the Ajax By-law Services division; AND WHEREAS Election Sign Deposit Programs are commonplace amongst Ontario municipalities as a means of improving compliance with Election Sign By-laws and recovering some of the cost of enforcement. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. That staff be directed to bring forward a by-law to amend the Town's Temporary Sign By-law and Election Sign By-law, no later than May 2023, to: - Prohibit the use of mobile advertising devices that include the use of amplified voice or music and/or digital or animated lights, posters or images; and, - Remove any option for an individual to pay a recovery fee to the Town for the return of an impounded sign. 2. That staff investigate options for an “Election Sign Deposit” program that would require election candidates to pay the Town a deposit that can be drawn upon by the Town for the removal of all illegally placed election signs in the Town, and provide a report on same to General Government Committee by the end of 2023.

WHEREAS to meet the needs of the community, the Town must invest in the purchase of vehicles and heavy equipment necessary for municipal operations; AND WHEREAS the Town may purchase vehicles or heavy equipment using funds from discretionary reserves, or through some form of financing; AND WHEREAS through the issuance of debentures, a type of long-term business debt, the impact of a major purchase can be spread out and lessen the immediate impacts to Town reserves; AND WHEREAS the Town has a policy in place which dictates that the maximum term for debt may not exceed the expected useful service life of an asset (the Tangible Capital Asset policy); AND WHEREAS reserves may be better leveraged for strategic investment over the life of the asset; NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: Staff be directed to report back to Council in June on the feasibility of purchasing vehicles and equipment over $100,000 through the issuance of debentures to ensure fulsome leveraging of Town reserves.

item: 9.3 Support for Bill 5 – Stopping Harassment and Abuse by Local Leaders Act
text: WHEREAS currently the most severe penalty that can be imposed on an elected official is suspension and loss of pay for 90 days, even in cases of workplace harassment or abuse; AND WHEREAS there is currently no process to remove an elected official from office, even in cases of confirmed workplace harassment or abuse; AND WHEREAS a fundamental, underlying principle of broadening diversity, equity and inclusion in politics rests on the assumption that the workplace is safe; AND WHEREAS Bill 5, the Stopping Harassment and Abuse by Local Leaders Act would require all elected officials to comply with the workplace violence and harassment policies of the municipality they represent, permit a municipality to direct the lntegrity Commissioner to apply to the court to vacate a member's seat for failing to comply with the municipality's workplace violence and harassment policies as well as restrict officials whose seat has been vacated from seeking re-election in any resulting by-election; AND WHEREAS at least 27 municipalities have formally endorsed and communicated public support for Bill 5, including Ottawa, Hamilton, London, Barrie, Orillia, and Richmond Hill; AND WHEREAS Bill 5 would both hold accountable and protect all municipal officials; NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: - Ajax Council express its support for Bill 5, Stopping Harassment and Abuse by Local Leaders Act; and - A copy of this motion be circulated to the Hon. Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, Patrice Barnes, MPP for Ajax, the Association of Municipalities of Ontario, Regional Council and Durham Region municipalities.
